In 2024, 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were living in poverty, using Canada's official poverty line, the Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base).

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (Alberta; persons under 18 years; MBM, 2023 base; percentage of persons in low income).
- **Reference period:** 2024, the latest year in the table.
- **Recent trend (same series):** 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024.
- **Another measure:** On the Low Income Measure after tax (v96520326), the 2024 rate is 13.9%. This is a different, relative measure, so the two figures are not interchangeable.

The average total income of Albertans aged 15 and over was **$66,100** in 2024, the latest year available. That average excludes people with zero income.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0239-01, vector v107680657. The series is Alberta; 15 years and over; Total - Gender; Total income; Average income (excluding zeros).
- **Recent years:** $66,000 in 2022, $66,300 in 2023 and $66,100 in 2024.
- **Median:** I did not retrieve the median for Alberta, which would be lower than the average. The same table has it.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024, the latest year available. The median after-tax income was **$85,300**.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Canadian Income Survey, table 11-10-0190-01.
- **Series:** v96414571 for total income and v96414651 for after-tax income. Both are for "Economic families and persons not in an economic family" in Alberta.
- **Reference period:** calendar year 2024. Median total income was $96,700 in 2022 and $98,400 in 2023.
- **Unit:** I did not check the unit. I assume current dollars, not adjusted for inflation.

This table measures economic families plus unattached individuals, which is the closest match to "household" in this table. It is not an exact household measure.

**About 12.8% of Alberta children (under 18) were in low income in 2024**, the latest year available. This uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Canadian Income Survey, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (Alberta; persons under 18 years; MBM, 2023 base; percentage of persons in low income).
- **Reference period:** 2024 (annual).
- **Recent trend:** 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024.

The rate depends on which poverty line is used. The Low Income Measure gives different figures, and I did not pull those.

Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration workers earned an average of **$1,883.03 per week** (all employees, including overtime) in August 2026, the latest month available.

- **Annual average, 2025:** $1,702.65 per week. The 2024 figure was $1,677.47 and the 2023 figure was $1,703.25.
- **Recent months:** $1,877.87 in June 2026 and $1,877.58 in July 2026.

**Sources**
- Monthly figures: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358. The series is Alberta; all employees; including overtime; NAICS 912, provincial and territorial public administration. The data are unadjusted for seasonality, and the reference period is August 2026, released 2026-10-29.
- Annual figures: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415, for 2023 to 2025.

These are weekly earnings, not hourly wages. I did not pull the hourly-paid or fixed-salary breakdowns. They are separate series in the same tables (for example, v1599034 for hourly-paid employees and v1587237 for salaried employees).

The 2025 annual average ($1,702.65) is well below the August 2026 monthly figure ($1,883.03). I did not check what accounts for that gap.

The average total income of Albertans aged 15 and over was **$66,100** in 2024, the latest year available. This is the average among people with income, so it excludes those with zero income.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0239-01, "Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source." It covers Alberta, ages 15 years and over, all genders, total income.
- **Vector:** v107680657
- **Reference period:** calendar year 2024. The 2023 figure was $66,300 and the 2022 figure was $66,000.

The figure is in current dollars, not adjusted for inflation. It is an average, so high earners pull it up. The median would be lower, and I did not look it up.

The latest figure is **$96,600**, the median total income of Alberta households in 2024.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Canadian Income Survey, table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96414571.
- **Series:** "Median total income, economic families and persons not in an economic family". This is the table's closest match to "household"; StatCan doesn't label it a household measure.
- **Reference period:** calendar year 2024, in current dollars. That is the latest year in the table.
- **Recent years:** $96,700 in 2022, $98,400 in 2023, $96,600 in 2024.

This is total income before tax. I didn't pull the after-tax median, which sits under "Median after-tax income" in the same table.

**12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were in low income in 2024, measured by the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), which is Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015, "Percentage of persons in low income". The reference period is calendar year 2024, the latest available.
- **Recent trend:** 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024. The low 2020–2021 figures came when pandemic income supports were in place.

Other low-income lines, such as the Low Income Measure, give different rates. I did not retrieve those.

Average weekly earnings for Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration were **$1,702.65 in 2025**, the latest annual figure.

- **Measure:** this is average weekly earnings for all employees, including overtime. Statistics Canada's category is "Provincial and territorial public administration"; for Alberta it covers only the provincial government.
- **Source:** Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH), table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415, annual, reference year 2025.
- **Recent years:** $1,703.25 in 2023, $1,677.47 in 2024, $1,702.65 in 2025.
- **Annualized:** $1,702.65 a week is roughly $88,500 a year. That is my own multiplication by 52 and is not a published figure.
- **Hourly wages and salaried-only earnings:** the series for hourly-paid employees (v1745591) and for fixed-salary employees (v1744055) returned no data for this industry in Alberta. I can't give an hourly wage for it.

The average total income of Albertans aged 15 and over was **$66,100** in 2024, the latest year available. The figure is in current dollars, before tax, and covers people with income (zeros excluded).

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01 (formerly 206-0052), "Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source." The series is v107680657 (Alberta; 15 years and over; Total - Gender; Total income; Average income, excluding zeros).
- **Reference period:** calendar year 2024. The table was last released on 2026-04-29.
- **Recent trend:**

| Year | Average total income |
|---|---|
| 2020 | $66,600 |
| 2021 | $67,500 |
| 2022 | $66,000 |
| 2023 | $66,300 |
| 2024 | $66,100 |

"Average income" can mean different things. This is total income from all sources, not employment income only, after-tax income or household income. I can pull median income, after-tax income or employment income for Alberta if you want one of those.

I couldn't retrieve a figure for Alberta's median household income, so I'm not giving one.
